decisions.what: zero-dep CommonJS Node CLI: pure modules (corpus/select/args) under src/ + a thin bin/ entry point; node:test only, no test framework
decisions.why: conductor-authored design under the SMOKE clock — no design-panel run. A ~200-line CLI has a forced architecture; the only real design choice is where the seam sits, and putting every decision in pure functions makes the Domain rules testable without spawning a process. Recorded as a DEVIATION: the DESIGN gate normally requires design-panel (600s budget), which does not fit a 25-min SMOKE window with ~8 min of work clock.

decisions.why: headless -p session cannot use Workflow (review-gated) so builders ran as direct Agent calls with no worktree isolation; strictly disjoint file scopes are the documented substitute, and a dependency-free split avoids ordering constraints between two concurrent builders

decisions.why: the documented command fails on Node 24 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the glob form runs all 48 tests green. Correcting a broken command string, NOT weakening a gate — the suite and its assertions are unchanged.

decisions.what: IMPROVEMENT RUN kickoff 2026-08-15: SPEC.md rewritten additively — the 2026-08-14 product spec is preserved verbatim and marked verified-done; a new 'Improvement run must-haves' section (I-1..I-6) scopes this run only
decisions.why: allocator auto-kickoff (source=allocator, brief 'harden tests, fix playbook items, polish docs — no new features'). The product spec is the floor this run must not break, not the work; keeping it verbatim makes a regression visible as a diff against a frozen block rather than as a rewrite.

decisions.why: headless allocator auto-kickoff has no user to confirm and SKILL.md defines no non-interactive behaviour for that gate — the exact house-rules gap this target's own RETRO (2026-08-14) proposed be settled. Recorded as a deviation rather than silently treated as confirmed.

decisions.what: New tests are admitted ONLY for measured mutation survivors, classified HOLE or BOUNDARY before any hardening
decisions.why: taste judge scored scope-fits-night 5/10 and named shortcut risk as load-bearing; the stress-test's toy-version trap landed on exactly this work type. Playbook L-031 (mutation-measure, don't read for gaps), L-029 (failable AND attributable), L-033 (HOLE vs BOUNDARY) are the guard. Test-count is not a deliverable.

decisions.what: Wave autotune raised k_current 3->4 on the second consecutive clean wave, but effective wave size stays 1
decisions.why: cycle.md Wave autotune: a clean wave (zero reverts, zero failed verifies) increments wave_streak, and at 2 it raises k_current and resets the streak. Recorded explicitly because it is INERT this run: effective size = min(k_current, gear cap 1) = 1, and gear 1 is fixed for the whole run (week_resets_at falls after stop_at). Carried so a future run on a healthier window inherits the learned number rather than re-deriving it.

decisions.what: HOLE/BOUNDARY classification of the 7 I-2a survivors is anchored to SPEC.md Domain rules, not to intuition: 5 HOLE, 1 BOUNDARY (M22), 1 DEFERRED to I-3 (M16). M16 produces no test this cycle even though it is completely unprotected.
decisions.why: The two non-hardened survivors are non-hardened for OPPOSITE reasons and the distinction is load-bearing. M22 has a rule and satisfies it - the mutant still exits 2 with clean stdout and a stderr message, and only the message wording changes, so a test would freeze prose no rule fixes and would false-reject an honest reword. M16 has NO rule at all: --list --json is the surface SPEC itself lists under OPEN AMBIGUITIES for item I-3, so writing a test now would silently promote today's NDJSON implementation to a promise and pre-empt the decision I-3 exists to make. Hardening every survivor would have been the easy, wrong answer.

decisions.what: Attribution at the gate is proven in the STRICT form — mutation applied with ALL FOUR new tests skipped must leave the suite green — rather than by removing one test at a time, and the harness carries a skip-sanity control.
decisions.why: Per-test isolation is ambiguous when two tests observe the same mutation: M12 drops the last --list entry, which is length-changing, so it trips the M13 order test too, and isolating M12 alone still shows fail=1. That reads like a failed attribution when it is really an expected overlap. The strict form asks the question that actually matters — does the mutation survive everything that existed before this cycle? — and it landed on exactly 52 pass / 0 fail, the pre-sweep baseline, for all four. The skip-sanity control exists because ATTRIBUTABLE is a PASS-shaped result: if --test-skip-pattern had silently matched everything, all four would have 'passed' vacuously.

decisions.what: The strict-attribution gate is measured on the TEST COUNT, not on node's skipped counter: --test-skip-pattern FILTERS matched tests out of the run (tests 58 -> 56, # skipped stays 0) rather than marking them skipped. A DENOMINATOR control was added to the harness alongside the cycle-5 SKIP-SANITY control.
decisions.why: Cycle 5's harness asserted skipped == <number of new tests> and this cycle that assertion failed while the substantive claim held (M21 + new tests filtered gave pass=56 fail=0, exactly the pre-cycle baseline). The assertion was measuring the reporter, not the claim. The fix STRENGTHENS the gate rather than relaxing it: the new DENOMINATOR control runs the pattern against PRISTINE source and requires it to remove exactly the tests added this cycle (58 -> 56, all green), which pins what was excluded; the old assertion only counted a field node never populates for filtered tests. Recorded because cycle 5's journal presents the skipped-count form as the precedent and a later cycle would otherwise re-derive this the hard way.

decisions.what: The --list line format and the --list --json NDJSON shape were settled by WRITING THE RULE, not by loosening the test that had been pinning them. I-3 closed six divergences where SPEC named three.
decisions.why: Cycle 5 surfaced a genuine tension and named both exits: a test now asserts --list's `<text> — <author>` line format, but no Domain rule promises it, so a test was acting as the de-facto spec. The two honest exits are write the rule or loosen the assertion to order-only; the dishonest one is leaving it. Chose to write the rule because --list is the flag people pipe into other tools — its line shape is a real contract in practice, and loosening would have deleted protection from a live surface to resolve a paperwork problem. Same reasoning applied to --list --json (M16): cycle 4 deferred hardening it precisely because no rule existed, so writing the NDJSON rule here is what unblocks hardening it later (new item I-8), rather than the rule being invented to bless whatever the code did.

decisions.what: A docs item was gated by EXECUTING the shipped binary — 36 behavioral checks with four discriminators — not by reading the prose it produced.
decisions.why: Every claim I-3 wrote is a claim about runtime behavior, so the docs are falsifiable exactly like code and the same evidence standard applies (hard rule 2). Reading the diff would only have confirmed the agent wrote what it was told; it could not have caught the agent transcribing a ruling the code does not actually honor. The discriminators exist because the naive checks are all passable by degenerate implementations: determinism alone is satisfied by an always-same-entry stub, so 7 seeds must reach 7 distinct aphorisms; a substring rule is only distinguishable from equality if the partial-author result set is required to EQUAL the full-name set. One imprecision was caught this way and fixed (the --list/--seed carve-out), which reading could not have surfaced.

decisions.what: I-7 closed as a superset of the two divergences it named: the --json HELP line was widened to cover the --list/NDJSON case even though the item's acceptance named only --author and --tag.
decisions.why: The --json line carried the IDENTICAL pre-I-3 defect the item exists to fix — a documentation surface describing only the non-list case — and it sits in the same file, in the same edit, at zero additional risk. Drawing the scope line so as to leave one of three known incompletenesses standing in the very file being opened to close that defect class would have been artificial rather than disciplined. Recorded here, and in the item's notes, rather than taken silently: widening an acceptance mid-cycle is a conductor call and must be visible as one. The opposite call was made for the --seed and --list lines and is the boundary that makes this one principled — both are incomplete (they omit the exotic-seed set and the --list-ignores-seed carve-out) but neither is MISLEADING, and README already carries the detail. The test is whether a reader would come away with a false belief, not whether the line is exhaustive.

decisions.what: A prose-only edit to a PRODUCT file was gated by byte-comparing everything outside the edited literal against HEAD, not by reading the diff or trusting the green suite.
decisions.why: HELP lives in src/args.js alongside parseArgs. A prose edit that also nudged parser logic would be invisible in a green suite if the nudge landed in a corner the 58 tests do not reach — and cycle 4's mutation sweep proved such corners existed in this exact file (M21, M22 both survived the whole suite). Reading the diff would only confirm the agent changed what it was told to; it cannot prove nothing ELSE moved. Splitting the file at the template-literal boundary and byte-comparing the 216-byte prologue and 2631-byte epilogue turns 'zero behaviour change' from a claim into a measurement, and the literal's own 362 -> 397 byte change simultaneously proves the item was not a no-op. This is the cycle-7 docs-are-falsifiable rule extended: when docs live INSIDE a product file, the scope claim needs proving as much as the content claim.

decisions.what: Wave autotune IS applied this cycle (wave_streak 0 -> 1) even though the item ran as a single direct Agent call rather than through the build-wave Workflow, reversing the reasoning cycle 8 used to skip it.
decisions.why: Cycle 8 declined to autotune on the ground that a direct Agent call is not a build-wave. That reasoning was really about the ITEM KIND -- cycle 8's item was docs, which is not a build-wave item under any dispatch mechanism. This cycle's item is kind 'test', i.e. build-class code, dispatched through the documented headless substitute for build-wave (Workflow is review-gated in a -p session, so direct Agent calls with strictly disjoint file scopes are the sanctioned fallback). Keying autotune on the dispatch MECHANISM rather than the work type would mean a headless run can never learn its wave size, which is not what the rule is for. Recorded rather than taken silently because it is a visible departure from last cycle's stated reasoning. INERT either way this run: effective wave size = min(k_current 5, gear cap 1) = 1, and gear 1 is structurally fixed because week_resets_at (1786942799) falls after stop_at (1786879464). The streak is being carried for a future run on a healthier window.

decisions.what: HARD RULE 5 DEVIATION BY A SUBAGENT, caught and cleaned: the builder created its mutation scratch copies under /opt/swarm/.scratch/ -- a SWARM path outside the runs/ and playbook/ write fence -- rather than under the system temp dir. It removed the copies itself; the conductor removed the leftover empty directory.
decisions.why: Worth recording because the prompt did NOT hand the agent a SWARM path: it was given target paths only, exactly as hard rule 5 requires. The agent reached a SWARM path anyway, almost certainly because the session cwd IS /opt/swarm, so a relative scratch path lands inside the fence by default. That makes it a STRUCTURAL hole rather than a prompt defect -- the fence is enforced by what agents are told, and cwd silently supplies what they were not told. No harm here (the writes were scratch copies of the target, nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ was touched, and the tree is clean), but the same reflex on a different task could write into SWARM tooling mid-run. Candidate lesson for the wrap-up distillation: builder prompts should name an explicit scratch location outside the repo, since 'do not write to SWARM' is not something the agent can honor if it does not know where it is standing. The conductor's own harness used os.tmpdir() and left nothing behind.

decisions.what: I-4 decomposed into I-4a (mechanical overclaim sweep) and I-4b (the ranked judgment artifact) — split by KIND OF CLAIM, not by risk band.
decisions.why: Cycle 9's handoff named two exits for I-4 not fitting gear 1's S-effort rule and preferred decomposition. The obvious decomposition — slice the corpus by risk band — is circular: the band assignment IS the deliverable, so you cannot use it to define the slices. Splitting by kind of claim gives two pieces that genuinely need DIFFERENT evidence: I-4b is a judgment that can only be cross-checked against an independent derivation, while I-4a is a mechanical grep-and-fix gated by byte-comparison. A seam that changes the verification method is a real seam; one that just halves the word count is not.

decisions.what: A judgment artifact was gated against a ranking SEALED TO DISK BEFORE the agent was dispatched, rather than by reading the output and agreeing with it.
decisions.why: Every prior gate this run had a command whose exit code carried the claim. A triage has none — it is 50 opinions about provenance, and reading it can only confirm that it reads well, which is precisely what a confabulated document also does. Writing the conductor's own high-risk list first (.swarm/runs/cycle-010-precommit.md) converts the check into a measurement: the agent could not have seen it, so overlap is evidence about the ranking rather than about the prose. It also cuts both ways by design — the agent's HIGH band found 4 entries the sealed list had NOT ranked high (#38 Wheeler, #39 Hopper, #45 Stroustrup, #48 Kay), and on inspection at least three are good catches, so the pre-commitment measured the conductor as much as the agent. Recorded honestly: the sealed list also contained an off-by-one (it named idx 39 as Wheeler; Wheeler is 38, 39 is Hopper), which affected only the informational Tier B tally, never the gate.

decisions.what: The document was ACCEPTED and then extended with a separately-attributed conductor addendum recording the four disagreements, rather than being sent back for a fix.
decisions.why: The disagreements are not defects the author could resolve — neither party has a source, so a revision round would only have produced a more confident document with the same epistemic basis, which is the opposite of what this deliverable is for. Row #45 is the sharp case: it asserts a specific checkable fact about what Stroustrup's FAQ SAYS (that he disclaims the foot-gun line) and row #46 leans on the same asserted FAQ. The conductor recalls the reverse. Recording that conflict at the top of the human's queue is strictly more useful than silently picking a winner, because the fact that two independent passes disagree about a primary source is itself the finding. Suppressing it to make the artifact look cleaner would have been the dishonest option.

decisions.what: removed the corpus.js attribution-policy claim outright rather than rewording it, and added a README Attribution section the item did not strictly require
decisions.why: Two judgment calls worth recording. (1) The header did not merely overstate — it described a hedging policy the file does not follow (1 of 50 hedged vs 8 HIGH-risk named attributions). A softened version ("we generally hedge...") would have preserved the false shape while sounding careful, which is the more dangerous failure: it reads as a considered disclosure. Deleting the policy claim and stating the actual epistemic status is the only honest option. (2) The README did NOT overclaim, so clause 1 of I-4a's acceptance did not oblige an edit there. I added the section anyway and am labelling it an addition rather than a correction: the triage document is the run's main deliverable to a human and was reachable only by reading source comments or the internal REPORT. A truthful corpus header that no user ever opens does not discharge the duty the item exists to serve.

decisions.what: I-5 satisfied via acceptance clause 2 (lossless archive + named reason for handoff), not clause 1 (full repair). The duplicate IDs were repaired outright; the 20-lesson cap breach was left open and handed to a human with a computed drop-list.
decisions.why: Clause 1 requires 'following the file's own documented overflow rule'. That rule drops ONE lesson per append invocation; there is no documented rule for shedding 11 at once, so claiming to have followed it would have been an overclaim of exactly the kind cycle 11 spent its budget removing from this repo. The extrapolation was computed anyway and measured: it drops L-003, L-006, L-007, L-008 and L-011 -- 5 of the file's [apply:]-bearing lessons, including the two most-applied lines in the ledger. A rule designed to shed one lesson produces a bad outcome at eleven. Deciding which 11 of 31 cross-run lessons to retire is a judgment about SWARM's own operating memory, made without a runnable validator; hard rule 5's fence exists for precisely this. Renumbering is reversible from the archive, deletion is not, so the reversible half was done and the irreversible half was handed off.

decisions.what: QA-full chosen over the taste pass for cycle 13, and the live-look stage declared not-applicable rather than run.
decisions.why: Both gate-4 passes were outstanding (last_full_qa_cycle and last_taste_cycle were both 0). QA-full wins the earlier slot because its findings land as kind:"fix" items that are IN scope for an improvement run, whereas taste findings land as kind:"feature"/"polish" and this run's spec makes every new feature a non-goal — a fundamental taste verdict would re-aim the clock at work the spec forbids. Live-look inspects a running product through a browser; this target is a Node CLI with no server or browser surface, so nothing could be inspected and nothing is claimed. Its cheap CLI analogue (output survives a pipe unchanged) was folded into the conductor harness as check S7.

decisions.what: The taste pass was dispatched through the qa-verify.js WORKFLOW rather than as a direct Agent call: the Workflow tool was permitted this session for the first time in 13 cycles.
decisions.why: Every cycle since kickoff recorded Workflow as review-gated in a -p session and used the documented direct-Agent fallback. The gate is evidently not a fixed property of headless sessions, so the sanctioned path was attempted first this cycle and it went through. Recorded because 13 journal entries assert the opposite and a future conductor reading them would otherwise skip the attempt on precedent. The correct standing behaviour is to ATTEMPT the workflow and fall back on refusal, not to assume the gate from history. Note the cost of using the real script on a CLI target: qa-verify.js has no CLI-shaped brief, so the agent was instructed to start a dev server on port 8137 and poll it with curl. It handled the mismatch honestly (ran it, confirmed via lsof that nothing listens, said so) but a browser-shaped brief is wasted budget on a CLI. Tool gap, journaled not fixed (hard rule 5).

decisions.what: The taste verdict was accepted while one of its headline numbers was REFUTED, and both halves are recorded rather than the finding being either discarded or silently corrected.
decisions.why: Finding 1 asserted 23 of 37 singleton tags; the true count is 21 (harness C1c). The tempting moves are both wrong: discarding the finding treats an arithmetic slip as if it falsified the observation, and quietly rewriting 23 to 21 erases that the agent miscounted, which is exactly the calibration signal a later reader needs when weighing its other numbers. The claim was therefore split — the ECHO behaviour was reproduced directly (8/8 pulls of --tag naming and --tag caching, 1 distinct output) and the distribution re-measured (30 of 37 tags hold <=2), so the finding stands on conductor-measured numbers while the agent's figure is marked refuted in the same file. Applied the same way to finding 2, in the opposite direction: its anecdote (first repeat at use 3) is not reproducible, but the underlying claim measured STRONGER than the agent could show from one session — 3000 simulated sessions put the mean first repeat at 9.60 against a closed-form 9.54, with the picker proven uniform so the cause is corpus size rather than a selection bug.

decisions.what: T-008 (deepen the corpus) was filed with deps on T-006 (the human attribution audit) instead of being queued as the highest-value taste finding.
decisions.why: It is the finding with the largest effect on the product's core complaint, and taking it would make an OPEN HIGH-severity known issue worse. KI-2 is open precisely because the existing 50 attributions are unaudited and 8 are high-risk; adding ~70 more unaudited quotes multiplies the unaudited surface in the same dimension a human has already been handed a queue for. Cycle 11 spent its budget removing overclaims about attribution quality from this repo, so bulk-adding unverified attributions the very next day would undo that work while looking like progress. Recorded as a dependency and a named judgment rather than a silent deprioritisation.

decisions.what: Headless builder dispatch: no /tmp worktrees
decisions.why: Dispatched T-012's builder into a /tmp worktree, per cycles 16-17 practice; the builder could not reach the path and reported the blocker instead of fabricating a diff. Re-dispatched into the target tree directly, which SKILL.md's headless rule prescribed all along. Recorded as KI-6 so the next cycle does not re-learn it.

decisions.what: Cycle 18's handoff said this repo was out of gear-1 work and cycle 19 should be a consolidation pass. It was not; a measurement item was picked instead, and it refilled the backlog with four admissible S-effort items.
decisions.why: The handoff's premise was that no BACKLOG item was admissible at gear 1, which was true. It does not follow that no WORK was admissible: gear 1 explicitly admits test triage, and cycle 4's mutation sweep predates every documentation guard this run built (T-009 Tag vocabulary, T-010/T-011 date recipe, I-4a Attribution). The unmeasured surface was created by this run itself and was therefore the least-measured thing in the repo. Recorded as a departure from a written handoff rather than taken silently. The distinction that makes this not busywork: the sweep asks a question with a real consequence attached -- T-007 (retagging) is live on the backlog and would falsify most of the README's tag numbers at once -- and the answer was NOT knowable by reading, which L-031 is precisely about.

decisions.what: The conductor's own verification harness failed on its first run and the failure was a HARNESS defect, not a finding: every mutant read as KILLED including the unmutated PRISTINE control.
decisions.why: Worth recording because the failure mode is the dangerous direction and it was caught by a control rather than by noticing. node --test defaults to the spec reporter, not TAP, so the harness's parse regexes returned null for tests/pass/fail; the survived predicate then evaluated false for EVERY copy and manufactured a KILLED verdict for all 21 mutants. Had the harness only checked claimed survivors, 'all survivors killed' would have read as a plausible refutation of the agent and the real findings would have been discarded. The PRISTINE control -- an unmutated whole-repo copy that must report 65/65 -- is what exposed it, which is exactly the job cycle 6 assigned to denominator/sanity controls after the same class of mistake (measuring the reporter rather than the claim). Fixed by forcing --test-reporter=tap and by making an unparseable run report UNPARSEABLE explicitly instead of falling through into a verdict. The gate was STRENGTHENED, not relaxed: a null parse can no longer produce any verdict at all.

decisions.what: 10 survivors classified HOLE and 3 BOUNDARY; the single most user-visible survivor (C3, the Flags table able to claim --tag is a substring match) is in the BOUNDARY set and is deliberately NOT being hardened.
decisions.why: C3 is a flat lie about shipped behaviour -- conductor-measured this cycle, --tag test exits 1 with empty stdout while --tag testing exits 0, so --tag is genuinely whole-tag. It is still a boundary, because the only available assertion is that the Effect cell contains a particular English phrase, which freezes one wording and false-rejects an honest reword. Cycle 4 classified M22 BOUNDARY on identical reasoning. Recorded loudly rather than buried because any reader of the survivor list will reasonably ask why the worst-looking item is being left alone. C7 (the 'Node 18+' claim) is the sharper case and the reason the classification step exists at all: no test in this repo can confirm the floor is 18, since the suite runs on whatever Node is installed, so a test asserting the string '18' would LOOK like verification while verifying nothing -- the exact failure class this run was chartered to remove. Settling it needs a CI matrix, which is a human decision.

decisions.what: Wave autotune NOT applied this cycle; wave_streak stays 1 and k_current stays 5.
decisions.why: Cycle 8 set the rule that autotune keys on the ITEM KIND, not the dispatch mechanism, and cycle 9 applied it to a kind:test item dispatched as a direct Agent call. T-013 is kind:qa -- a measurement that produced a survivor list and changed no product or test file -- which is not build-class work under any dispatch mechanism, the same reason cycle 8 declined to autotune on a docs item. Inert either way: effective wave size = min(k_current 5, gear cap 1) = 1.

decisions.what: Removed 9 untracked scratch files (create_test.js, edit_readme.js, final_report.json and kin) left in the SWARM root at /opt/swarm by cycle-17 and cycle-18 builder dispatches.
decisions.why: SECOND occurrence of the structural hole cycle 9 recorded and named as a candidate lesson: agents are handed target paths only, per hard rule 5, but the session cwd IS /opt/swarm, so any relative scratch path lands inside the write fence by default. Cycle 9 said the fix is for dispatch prompts to name an explicit scratch location, since 'do not write to SWARM' is not something an agent can honor if it does not know where it is standing. That fix was recorded but never made standing, and it recurred twice. This cycle's dispatch DID name an explicit scratch path (/opt/targets/aphorism-cli/.swarm/scratch/, chosen over /tmp because KI-6 established /tmp is unreachable from the subagent sandbox) and the agent left nothing behind -- harness control CTRL-SCRATCH confirms the directory is gone and CTRL-TREE confirms the target tree carries only cycle-019 artifacts. Nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ was ever touched; the debris was inert scratch. Promoted to KI-7 so it stops being re-learned once per run.

decisions.what: Accepted the T-014 guard as-is despite a measured false-rejection case (a blank line between a band heading and its table fails the suite), and filed it as T-018 rather than sending the item back.
decisions.why: The failure direction is what decides this. T-012 and the whole A7/A8 family are guards that go QUIET on an innocuous edit -- they hide. This one fails loudly and names the parse as the cause, so it cannot hide anything; a reader who trips it is told exactly what happened. Measured, not assumed: reformat alone gives fail 1, and reformat plus a row deletion is still KILLED, so the guard is not disarmed by the reformat. Sending the item back would spend a gear-1 cycle re-opening a passing acceptance to improve ergonomics, when three higher-value HOLEs (T-015..T-017) are still open.

decisions.what: The T-015 gate's decisive check is one no acceptance clause asked for: mutate the CORPUS, update the README to the new true numbers, and require the suite to stay GREEN.
decisions.why: Every other check this cycle asks whether a WRONG README is caught. None of them can distinguish a guard that derives its expectations from the corpus from one that hardcodes 16/4/12/21, because both catch a wrong number today. That distinction is the entire point of the item: T-007 (retagging) is live on the backlog and would change all four numbers at once, and a hardcoded guard would then fire on a CORRECT README -- a false rejection that a maintainer resolves by deleting the guard, which is worse than never having written it. The consistent-change check is the only form that separates the two: I gave one entry the existing tag `performance` (4 -> 5 occurrences), independently re-derived the new truth (ge5 4->5, band2-4 12->11, ge2/eq1/distinct unchanged), edited the README to match, and required 68/68. A hardcoded guard fails there. It passed, and the paired stale-README half fails at 3 tests, so the guard is provably corpus-derived in both directions.

decisions.what: SCOPE.SCRATCH is recorded as a FAILED gate check even though the item passed, and the gate was NOT re-run to a 29/29.
decisions.why: The builder deleted its mutation copies but left an empty .swarm/scratch directory, so the check I authored (directory removed) failed while the claim it exists to protect (no scratch content leaked) held -- measured at 0 files inside, and git status showed no untracked scratch. The tempting move is to relax the check to 'directory is empty' and re-run for a clean sheet, which would be opening a gate by weakening it. The honest record is that the control failed as written, what it did and did not establish, and that the conductor removed the directory by hand. It is also a housekeeping control rather than one of T-015's four acceptance clauses, all of which passed FAILABLE and ATTRIBUTABLE -- so the item is done and the control is a KI-7 data point, which is the third occurrence of that structural hole and now has an empty-directory variant.

decisions.what: Conductor probe N2 found a survivor one level above the item's scope -- deleting an entire band table leaves the suite green -- and it was FILED as T-019 rather than fixed inside this cycle.
decisions.why: It is the T-014/A7 blindness one level up: T-014 made each band table's rows bidirectional and T-015 made each heading's cardinality checkable, but both iterate only the bands that are PRESENT, so a band that stops being claimed is never examined and every remaining stated fact is still true. Fixing it inside T-015 would have meant widening a passing acceptance to cover a mechanism it does not have (an expected-band-partition check is a different design, not an extra assertion), and the cycle-8 boundary applies: widening is principled when the same defect sits in the same edit at zero extra risk, and artificial when it needs new machinery. Filed at priority 5, below T-016/T-017, because a whole table vanishing is a much less likely edit than the single-row and cross-file cases and -- unlike A7 -- it is not on T-007's path, since retagging edits rows rather than deleting tables.

decisions.what: All three of T-016's claims were guarded; C2 was NOT dropped, even though the item explicitly authorised dropping it honestly.
decisions.why: The item's permission was conditional -- "may honestly be dropped if it proves fiddly to parse; say so rather than forcing it" -- and the condition did not hold. I checked before dispatch rather than after: docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md parses structurally into 50 rows with ids 0-49 distinct and risk bands HIGH 8 / MEDIUM 16 / LOW 26, keyed on the first cell being a bare integer, which excludes the header and separator rows without depending on any wording. A conditional escape hatch that is taken without testing its condition is just a dropped requirement with a citation attached. Recorded because the opposite call -- dropping C2 and citing the item's own words -- would have looked equally authorised in the journal.

decisions.what: The R2 consistent-change check, invented at cycle 21 against the corpus, was generalised this cycle to THREE different kinds of ground truth: a source module (corpus.length), another document in the repo (the triage doc's HIGH count), and the filesystem itself (Layout paths).
decisions.why: Cycle 21 established that every other check asks whether a WRONG README is caught, and a guard hardcoding today's numbers passes all of them -- only changing the real artifact and the README TOGETHER, and requiring green, separates the two. T-016 is the first item where that question has three different answers, because its three claims are checked against three unrelated sources, and a guard could plausibly be derived for one and hardcoded for another. So the pair was run three times rather than once: corpus 50->51 with the README updated stays green (stale half fails naming C1); a triage row flipped MEDIUM->HIGH with the README updated stays green (stale half fails naming C2); a real new file plus its Layout line stays green (a Layout line for a file never created fails naming C6). All six halves landed as required. This matters concretely because T-007 (retagging) and any future corpus growth would walk a hardcoded guard straight into a false rejection on a CORRECT README, which a maintainer resolves by deleting the guard.

decisions.what: Conductor probe N1 found a false-rejection case and it was FILED as T-020 rather than fixed in-cycle; the probe existed only because the builder volunteered the weakness in its own report.
decisions.why: Two things worth recording. (1) The classification: rewording the Attribution aside to "8 of the 50 entries carry a rating of HIGH" -- every number still true -- fails the suite at 71/70/1 because the extraction takes the digit nearest BEFORE the marker and, with the em dashes gone, 50 sits nearer to HIGH than 8 does. That is a false REJECTION of an honest edit, not a silent hole: it fails loud and names the C2 test, so a maintainer who trips it is told what happened. Same direction, and therefore the same LOW classification, as T-018 at cycle 20. (2) The provenance: the builder's report named this exact edge case under "things I was unsure about" instead of omitting it, and that is the only reason I probed the dash-free word order at all. An honest uncertainty note converted directly into a measured backlog item, which is the behaviour the dispatch prompt asked for and got.

decisions.what: The conductor gate was REPAIRED mid-verification rather than reported as a 12-fail result: harness v1 sniffed failing-test identity by looking for TAP "not ok" while running node's DEFAULT reporter, so every by-name attribution read false and eight substantively-passing checks were rendered as failures. v2 runs every mutation under --test-reporter=tap and attributes each failure to a test by name.
decisions.why: Hard rule 2 cuts both ways: a gate that cannot distinguish "the suite failed" from "the NEW test failed" is not evidence, and shipping its output as a verdict would have been the mirror image of trusting an agent. Repairing the instrument is not weakening the gate -- v2 asks strictly MORE than v1 did (it now requires the failure to carry the T-017 name, where v1 only counted failures) and the item passes the stronger form. Recorded because the tempting alternative -- reading fail=1 as "close enough, the item works" -- is exactly the reasoning the evidence-or-silence rule exists to forbid.

decisions.what: T-017 is accepted on the README-LITERAL side of its comparison only. The binary-side mutations (separator, reversed order, dropped line) fail the new test but are NOT attributable to it: the pre-existing test "--list preserves corpus order (first and last line match)" already kills all three.
decisions.why: The honest accounting of what a new test buys is what it catches that nothing else does, not what it happens to notice. Reporting the binary-side kills as T-017 value would have inflated the item threefold. What is genuinely new -- and what survivor C5 actually named -- is that the README's format LITERAL is now pinned to real runtime behaviour: mutate it to a pipe, or merely delete the spaces around the em dash, and the whole rest of the suite sits green at 71/71/0 while this one test fails by name.

decisions.what: The gate's decisive check used a README LAYOUT THAT DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS REPO -- a three-band Tag vocabulary section (10+, 5-9, 2-4) -- rather than only the two-band layout the item was written against.
decisions.why: Every acceptance-shaped check asks whether deleting a band table is caught, and a guard hardcoding 'there must be a 5+ table and a 2-4 table' passes all of them, because it does catch today's deletion. The two readings only separate on a README the repo has never had. T-007 (retagging) is live on the backlog and could legitimately change the band boundaries or the NUMBER of bands, at which point a hardcoded guard fires on a CORRECT README -- a false rejection a maintainer resolves by deleting the guard, which is worse than never having written it. So the pair was run on the unfamiliar layout: the correct three-band README stays green at 73/73, and deleting the MIDDLE band kills naming T-019 alone and is attributable at 72/72/0. The middle-band mutation is also the only one that proves the fix is not riding on the pre-existing zero-band sanity assertion, since two band tables are still standing when it fires. This is the cycle-21/22 R2 consistent-change method extended from 'change the artifact' to 'change the artifact's SHAPE'.

decisions.what: Two gate checks FAILED and the item was accepted anyway; neither was re-run to a manufactured clean sheet, and the more interesting of the two was proven NOT to belong to the item under test.
decisions.why: R3.GREEN failed: rewording a band heading's lead-in, with every digit and row intact, fails the suite. The tempting reading of a red check on a verification gate is that the item under test caused it. That was measured rather than assumed (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-probe-R3.txt) -- the identical rewording fails identically against HEAD's test file, which contains no T-019 test at all, and the T-019 assertion itself stays green under all three rewording variants. So it is a PRE-EXISTING fragility in the T-014 heading-count test that this cycle's gate happened to surface, filed as T-022, and the honest record is a failed control plus its attribution rather than either a quietly relaxed check or a defect charged to the wrong item. S3.SCRATCH failed for the second time in four cycles (KI-7). Both are recorded as failures as authored, per the cycle-21 precedent: relaxing a control and re-running for 23/23 would be opening a gate by weakening it.

decisions.what: The conductor's own harness broke on its first run (a corpus-mutation helper sliced off a string's opening quote and produced a SyntaxError) and was repaired mid-verification.
decisions.why: Third cycle in a row where the instrument failed before the item did (cf. cycle 19's reporter parse bug, cycle 23's TAP attribution bug). Worth recording because the failure direction was SAFE this time -- a SyntaxError is loud and unmissable, unlike cycle 19's bug which silently manufactured a KILLED verdict for every mutant including the pristine control. The repair changed the mutation helper only; no check was relaxed, and the acceptance checks A3/A4 had already passed before the R1 helper was ever reached, so the repair could not have been motivated by a result it wanted to change.

decisions.what: The prose-anchor guard family is now FIVE items deep (T-018, T-020, T-021, T-022, T-023) and is being treated as a standing design finding, not as five separate bugs. Every README guard this run has built extracts a number by anchoring to a position or a literal in English prose, and every fix so far has NARROWED the anchor rather than removed it. T-023 is filed with an explicit BOUNDARY option rather than an automatic harden.
decisions.why: Recorded as a decision so it reaches RETRO as one lesson instead of five backlog corpses. The failure direction has been safe every time -- these guards reject a correct README loudly rather than passing a wrong one silently -- but a maintainer's cheapest escape from a false rejection is deleting the guard, so the cumulative risk is that the whole family gets removed at once. The honest generalisation is that a documentation guard should extract from STRUCTURE (tables, rows, tokens) and only ever from prose when the prose token carries mathematical meaning; where prose is genuinely ambiguous, SPEC I-2's BOUNDARY classification is the right outcome, not another narrowing.

decisions.what: RECYCLE cycle taken at cycles_since_recycle 25 with four admissible S-effort items sitting on the board, and it is NOT counted against counters.consecutive_no_value (stays 0, not incremented to 1).
decisions.why: Two calls worth recording. (1) The recycle was TAKEN rather than deferred. Hard rule 7's trigger is a context-length proxy, not a workload signal, so "there is still work" is never a reason to skip it -- deferring to finish T-018 would spend the recycle's whole purpose (a fresh session re-orienting from disk) to save one 5-minute pacer interval, and this run has ~15.8h left, so the interval is free. This is the FIRST recycle of the run; cycles 1-25 ran without one. (2) The churn breaker was NOT incremented. Read literally, "a cycle with no verified-value outcome increments it" would fire here, because a recycle produces no verified value BY CONSTRUCTION. But the counter exists to detect a target that cannot make progress -- at >=2 it forces a work-type switch, at >=4 a consolidation pass, at >=6 it STALLS the target, and only a manual user edit un-stalls it. Charging a conductor-mandated pause to that ladder would mean a long run walks itself toward a false stall on its own housekeeping. Cycle 25 verified T-022 and reset the counter to 0; nothing about this cycle is evidence that the target has stopped producing value. Recorded rather than taken silently because it is a departure from the rule's literal text, and a later conductor reading only the counter would otherwise see a gap it cannot explain.

decisions.what: The pre-dispatch baseline REDEFINED what T-018's acceptance clause could honestly mean, and the gate demanded strictly more than the clause as written.
decisions.why: T-018's acceptance said a blank line must leave the suite green 'while a row deletion under that reformatted heading still fails'. Cycle 20 had recorded that reformat+row-deletion was 'still KILLED' and read that as the guard still working. Re-measuring at the current 73-test suite before dispatch (.swarm/runs/cycle-027-baseline.txt) showed that reading was wrong: reformat+row-deletion (B4) fails with the IDENTICAL signature as reformat ALONE (B1), 73/72/1 naming only the T-019 union test, whereas a row deletion with no reformat (B5) fails at 73/71/2 and names the band-contents assertion too. The whole band is invisible, so the suite is reporting the PARSE failure and the deleted row is masked. A fix that made the reformat green while leaving detection broken would therefore have satisfied the acceptance clause exactly as written, and the item would have closed on a technically-true reading. The gate's requirement became: under a reformatted heading, a row deletion must produce the SAME signature as one with no reformat at all. It does -- A7 and A8 both land 73/71/2 with identical failing test names. The general point worth carrying: an acceptance clause written from an earlier cycle's measurement can go stale, and re-measuring the DEFECT before dispatch is what catches it. Inheriting cycle 20's figure would have hidden this.

decisions.what: Took exit (a) -- fix T-018 narrowly -- and filed the structural re-shape as T-024 for a healthier window. The deciding argument is NOT that (b) did not fit gear 1; it is that T-018 was never a member of the prose-anchor family.
decisions.why: The cycle-26 handoff framed the judgment as (a) narrow fix vs (b) re-shape the extraction to read structure and close two or three siblings at once, with gear 1's S-effort rule as the tiebreak. Reading the extractor settled it on the merits before the budget argument was needed: extractBandTablesFromReadme already locates a band STRUCTURALLY -- the `| Tag | Count |` header row plus the `|---|---|` separator -- and reads only band-bound digits (`5+`, `2-4`) from the heading, which the cycle-25 finding explicitly permits because those digits carry mathematical meaning. Its defect was an ADJACENCY requirement, not a prose anchor, and the fix removes a requirement rather than narrowing an anchor. So T-018 is not a sixth member of the family and closing it narrowly does not add to the cumulative deletion risk cycle 25 named. The family stays T-020/T-021/T-023 and the re-shape is filed as T-024 (M-effort, unreachable this run) so the finding survives as an actionable item rather than only as retro prose. Recorded because 'it did not fit the gear' would have been an available and much weaker justification for the same action.

decisions.what: Gate check A9 is recorded as FAILED AS AUTHORED and was NOT rewritten to pass, even though a follow-up probe proved its substantive claim holds and proved the red does not belong to the item.
decisions.why: A9 asserted that a wrong ROW COUNT under a reformatted heading still fails loud AND that the band-contents assertion is what fires. It failed loud (73/72/1) but named a different guard, 'README tag counts must match corpus'. The predicate encoded a wrong belief of mine about which test owns cell values: the band-contents assertion computes expected membership from CORPUS counts, so editing a table's stated number does not move that tag out of its band there -- a separate pre-existing test owns the cell value. The probe (.swarm/runs/cycle-027-probe-A9.txt) settles attribution in four cells: fixed parser gives 73/72/1 with and without the reformat, and HEAD's parser gives the same 73/72/1 without the reformat -- three identical cells, so the reformat is not what changes anything. The only cell that differs is HEAD+reformat at 73/71/2, where the extra failure is exactly the parse-failure noise T-018 removes; the fix strictly REDUCES noise here. Rewriting the predicate after seeing the result would have been coding to the outcome, which is the mirror image of what this run exists to prevent, so the failed check stands with its attribution attached (cycle-21 and cycle-24 precedent). Side finding, recorded rather than back-edited: cycle 24's note that band assertion 2 'also catches a row whose count was edited without moving it' is imprecise -- assertion 2 catches a tag that does not belong in its band; the cell VALUE is caught elsewhere.

decisions.what: The allowlist gap (KI-5) is PATH-FORM sensitive, which two cycles of journal entries had generalised wrongly: `bin/swarm-notify.sh poll` runs, `/opt/swarm/bin/swarm-notify.sh poll` is REFUSED.
decisions.why: Cycles 25 and 26 both recorded that notify poll 'RAN clean' and cycle 26 promoted it to a property -- 'one sample was luck, two is a property: notify is reachable, budget and playbook are not'. This cycle the absolute-path form was tried first and refused; the relative form then ran clean against the same binary. So the reachable/unreachable split is not a property of the SCRIPT, it is a property of the literal command string matched against the allowlist. bin/swarm-budget.sh was attempted in BOTH forms this cycle and refused in both, so its unreachability is genuine and KI-5's substance stands. Recorded because a future conductor reading cycles 25-26 would conclude the script is what matters and could log a spurious probe failure after invoking a reachable tool by its absolute path.

decisions.what: T-021's fix was REJECTED and reverted after passing all 22 gate checks, including both halves of its own acceptance, both discriminators, and every loudness check. The rejection rests entirely on a follow-up probe the acceptance never asked for.
decisions.why: The fix (scan every '### ' heading, strip backticks, take the FIRST carrying both the --list token and the word 'behaviour') did exactly what the item asked and removed the false rejection. What it also did was introduce FIRST-MATCH THEFT, and the consequence is in the dangerous direction. Probe .swarm/runs/cycle-028-probe-B4.txt, cell P3: an earlier decoy heading carrying both tokens, whose section holds a correct-looking `<text> - <author>` literal, lets the REAL section's format literal be mutated to something FALSE and the suite passes at 73/73/0. Cell P4 proves HEAD catches that identical input at 73/72/1. So the fix converts a case HEAD caught into a case nothing catches. Every member of this guard family (T-018 c20, T-020 c22, T-021 c23, T-022 c24, T-023 c25, T-025 c27) has been a LOUD false rejection, and the standing classification rule is that loud-and-wrong is the safe direction while silent-and-wrong is the failure class this run was chartered to remove. Trading the first for the second is strictly worse than leaving T-021 open, so the item goes back to todo at attempts 1 rather than being accepted with a follow-up filed. Recorded at length because the tempting reading of 22/22 is acceptance: the gate as authored was SATISFIED, and only a probe motivated by the builder's own uncertainty note found the reason not to.

decisions.what: The gate demanded attribution by ASSERTION MESSAGE rather than by failing-test name, because the pre-dispatch baseline proved test-name attribution could not settle this item.
decisions.why: Second cycle running that the pre-dispatch baseline redefined what an acceptance clause could honestly mean (cf. cycle 27, T-018). T-021's clause reads: a mutated format literal under the reformatted heading must still FAIL. Baseline cells B1 and B3 measured 73/72/1 naming the IDENTICAL test for reformat-alone and for reformat-plus-mutated-literal -- the heading parse failure masks the literal mutation, so the clause is ALREADY satisfied at HEAD and is satisfiable by a fix that never restores detection. The gate therefore captured the assertion TEXT from the TAP output and classified each red as HEADING-PARSE, LITERAL-PARSE or SEPARATOR-MISMATCH, requiring the red half to be SEPARATOR-MISMATCH. Checks A2 and A2b are the pair that makes the point: identical signatures, different causes. This is the cycle-27 A7-equals-A8 method pushed one level finer, from test identity down to failure cause, and it generalises -- any guard whose parse failure and whose substantive failure land in the same test cannot be verified by name alone.

decisions.what: A harness imprecision is recorded rather than back-edited: the gate's `reason` classifier is only meaningful on a RED run.
decisions.why: The SEPARATOR-MISMATCH branch keys on text including '--list output', which also appears in the passing test's NAME, so every GREEN run reports reason=SEPARATOR-MISMATCH spuriously (visible in probe cells P2, P3, P5). It affected no verdict: every gate check that asserted on `reason` also asserted a red signature (C1, A1b, A2, A2b, L1, L2, B2, B3), and P3's verdict rests on its 73/73/0 signature, not on its reason field. Recorded because cycle 19's harness bug -- a parse failure silently manufacturing a verdict -- is the precedent for treating instrument defects as findings in their own right, and because a later reader scanning the probe output would otherwise see 'SEPARATOR-MISMATCH' next to a green run and mistrust the whole file. Fourth cycle in this run where the instrument needed comment (cf. c19 reporter parse, c23 TAP attribution, c24 mutation helper).

decisions.what: T-025 was classified HOLE and hardened, REFUTING the BOUNDARY premise it was filed with. The deciding evidence is a probe of the item's own central factual claim, which no acceptance clause asked for.
decisions.why: The item was filed at cycle 27 asserting that widening the scan 'trades a loud false rejection for a possible silent mis-parse'. That is a factual claim about what a widened scan does, and it had never been run -- it was inherited reasoning from T-018's constraint set. Cycle 28 is the precedent that makes this the load-bearing step: there a fix passed 22/22 and was rejected only because a probe went looking for the silent case, so the same standard has to cut BOTH ways -- a probe that can reject a passing item must also be allowed to rescue a mis-filed one. 18 cells (6 README variants x 3 scan variants, PRISTINE control 73/73/0) found no silent hole under either widening, and the widened scans were LOUDER on every wrong README (73/72/1 -> 73/71/2). Had I taken the filed classification on trust, the honest-looking outcome would have been a BOUNDARY comment restating an argument the measurement contradicts -- a documented non-fix that reads as diligence.

decisions.what: The conductor sealed its own classification AND its own preferred fix shape to disk before dispatch (.swarm/runs/cycle-029-precommit.md); the builder independently reached both. A labelling error in the conductor's harness is recorded rather than back-edited.
decisions.why: Cycle 10 established that a judgment deliverable cannot be gated by reading it and agreeing -- that is exactly what a confabulated document also survives. The pre-commitment converts agreement into a measurement: the builder could not see the file, so its arrival at HOLE *and* at the moderate stop-at-band-token shape (rather than the maximal widening) is evidence about the conclusion rather than about the prose. The seal also named in advance what would make BOUNDARY acceptable -- a measured one -- so the pre-commitment could not function as a rubber stamp for the answer I preferred. Recorded honestly: the seal names an error in my own probe, where R4 was labelled `wrong: true` when every number in it is true. It could not have corrupted the verdict (a silent hole requires conservative RED and R4 is conservative GREEN) but the label is wrong in the source and stands uncorrected there, per the cycle-21/24/27 precedent on failed or imprecise controls.

decisions.what: The gate's 20/20 was NOT treated as sufficient: probe N1 was run afterwards against the one wrong-README shape every gate variant shared a blind spot for -- an ORPHAN table whose preceding heading carries no band token.
decisions.why: Every wrong-README variant in the gate had a band-token heading, so the shipped stop rule could always see the boundary it was being tested on. That is a gate measuring the cases it was designed around. The orphan shape is the one the stop rule structurally CANNOT see, so it is where a silent hole would live if one existed. Both orphan variants -- one with unrelated rows, one with plausible-but-incomplete 5+ rows chosen to look like a successful theft -- are caught LOUD at 74/72/2 against HEAD's 73/72/1. The reason is structural and was documented by the builder rather than leaned on silently: both consumer tests assert EXACT set equality between a band's corpus-derived expected tags and its table's actual rows, so a mis-attached table carries rows derived from a different heading's range and cannot coincide. Cycle 28's lesson stated generally: the decisive probe is the one the acceptance never asked for.

decisions.what: T-021 was accepted WITH a new false rejection that this run created, filed as T-028, rather than reported as a clean 9/9. Gate cell N1: a README carrying a second '### ' heading that also names --list and 'behaviour', with EVERY claim in both sections true, is GREEN at HEAD (74/74/0) and RED on the fixed tree (78/77/1, AMBIGUITY).
decisions.why: Every other member of this guard family was a PRE-EXISTING fragility that a gate happened to surface. This one the run introduced, and an honest accounting has to say so in those words rather than let 9/9 imply nothing was given up. It is still the right trade, and the argument is measured rather than asserted: the ONLY alternative anyone has implemented is first-match-wins, which cycle 28 measured into a SILENT HOLE (a decoy section with a correct-looking literal lets the real literal be mutated to something false at 73/73/0). This repo's standing classification is that loud-and-wrong is the safe direction and silent-and-wrong is the failure class the run was chartered to remove, so trading a silent hole for a loud, self-describing rejection travels the right way even though the rejection is new. Filed rather than decided because there is a real case that two headings both claiming to describe --list behaviour IS ambiguous documentation and failing loud is correct -- that is my lean, and it deserves a measurement rather than my say-so.

decisions.what: The conductor's own instruments failed THREE separate times this cycle -- once in the pre-dispatch baseline and twice in the verification gate -- and every failure is recorded with its repair rather than silently corrected. This is the FIFTH CONSECUTIVE CYCLE in which the instrument broke before the item did (cf. c19 reporter parse, c23 TAP attribution, c24 mutation helper, c28 reason classifier).
decisions.why: The three failures are worth separating because they differ in DIRECTION, which is the property that decides how dangerous a harness bug is. (1) BASELINE, cell P3: the decoy-insertion and literal-mutation helpers were composed in the wrong order, so the mutation landed on the DECOY's format literal and left the real section correct. The cell read GREEN -- 'HEAD does not catch the theft case' -- which is a PASS-SHAPED FALSE RESULT and the dangerous direction: taken at face value it would have contradicted cycle 28's finding and undercut the entire reason for rejecting attempt 1. It was caught only because the cell's expected reading was written down before it ran. The repair added a postcondition that the mutation must be present in the section the test actually reads; the pre-existing 'the bytes changed' guard passed the vacuous version, which is precisely why a byte-diff is not an applied-mutation check. (2) GATE, classifier precedence: LITERAL-PARSE was tested before SEPARATOR-MISMATCH on the substring 'format literal', but the separator assertion's own message QUOTES the literal it compared against, so three substantively-correct cells (A2, A3, P3) were rendered FAIL. Loud direction. (3) GATE, classifier character class: the repair used [^.]{0,60} between 'could not find a' and 'format literal', but the placeholder in that message is `<text>...<author>`, which contains dots -- so L2 flipped to FAIL. Also loud. Both gate repairs made the classifier STRICTER, not looser: LITERAL-PARSE now requires the could-not-find phrasing only the real parse-miss carries, so it can no longer absorb a separator mismatch, and an unspecific match is reported as its own LITERAL-PARSE-UNSPECIFIC label instead of being folded into a verdict. That is the cycle-23 rule -- repairing an instrument that cannot distinguish two outcomes is not the same as relaxing a check that can -- and the distinction is what keeps three mid-verification edits from being three chances to code to the result.

decisions.what: The sealed pre-commitment was reached independently by the builder, and two discriminators it did NOT contain established that the fix re-shapes the extraction structurally rather than narrowing it a seventh time. T-024's scope was reduced from three prose-anchored extractions to two on that evidence.
decisions.why: Cycle 25's standing finding is that every README guard this run built anchors an extraction to a position or literal in English prose, that every fix so far had NARROWED the anchor, and that the cumulative risk is a maintainer deleting the whole family at once. The distinction between 'narrowed' and 're-shaped' therefore has to be measurable, or the finding is just a mood. Gate cells D1 and D2 are that measurement and the builder was never told about them: D1 rewrites the heading as 'behaviour of `--list`' -- both tokens, different word ORDER -- and D2 appends trailing punctuation. Both are GREEN on the fixed tree while HEAD rejects both at 74/73/1. A fix that had merely made the backticks optional in a fixed-string regex passes the item's acceptance and FAILS D1 and D2, so the two readings genuinely separate. Recorded because 'this one is a re-shape, not a narrowing' would otherwise be exactly the kind of self-serving classification this run keeps catching in other places.

decisions.what: The conductor classified T-026 BOUNDARY, wrote the comment, passed its own 7/7 gate, and was REFUTED by the independently dispatched classifier. The comment was reverted, the item reopened, and the classifier's fix adopted as the recorded answer.
decisions.why: This is the pre-commitment method doing the job it exists for, against the conductor rather than against an agent. The seal written before dispatch named its own refutation condition -- a rule that turns the "Node 18+" README green, keeps orphan and sibling-theft red, and adds no NEW English anchor -- precisely so the cheap verdict I was predisposed toward could be falsified rather than defended. All three clauses were met. The clause I got wrong is (c): I argued the "N tags" phrase would be a seventh prose anchor, and never checked whether it was ALREADY mandatory. It is -- cell V9:HEAD shows a band heading stripped of that phrase is already RED at HEAD, enforced by a pre-existing test. So the fix reuses an anchor the file already demands instead of adding one, and my central objection does not apply. Recorded at length because the tempting move was available and cheap: my gate was 7/7, the item would have closed, and the counter would have read two landed items instead of one.

decisions.what: KI-8 has a THIRD leak channel and it is the conductor's own doing: the classifier read the conductor's uncommitted BOUNDARY comment out of `git diff` on a tracked file, while the conductor's hash-sealed pre-commitment sat safely outside the sandbox.
decisions.why: The mitigation this cycle introduced was sound and it was defeated by impatience, not by its design. I applied my classification to test/readme-tags.test.js while the classifier was still running, so `git diff` handed it my conclusion and my reasoning verbatim. Cycles 31 and 32 leaked through .swarm/runs/; this is a channel neither anticipated, and it is worse in kind, because a tracked-file diff is something any agent may legitimately inspect to check whether it caused a change -- which is exactly why this one did. The rule that follows is concrete: while an independent agent is running, the conductor must not write its own conclusions into the working tree. The direction of harm was benign here only by luck -- the classifier disagreed anyway and disclosed the read unprompted, and that disclosure is the only reason the conductor's error was caught rather than committed.

decisions.what: T-028 closed and T-026 reopened on the SAME evidential standard: two independent passes agreeing closes an item, two independent passes disagreeing does not.
decisions.why: Both items were decided by a conductor measurement and an agent classification run blind to it. On T-028 they agreed on the verdict by refuting DIFFERENT candidate fixes -- the conductor a content-based disambiguator, the classifier a shape-based one -- and two independent routes to the same silent hole is a materially stronger basis than either alone. On T-026 they disagreed, and the disagreement resolved against the conductor on measurement. Applying the same rule in both directions is what keeps the first result from being self-congratulation: the standard was fixed before either answer was known.

decisions.what: The forced work-type switch was honoured by running the cycle with NO builder: the conductor measured, one agent classified, and no agent was asked to write code.
decisions.why: The churn breaker bound at consecutive_no_value 2, and cycles 31 and 32 were both "dispatch a builder at readme-tags.test.js, gate it, reject it". A third dispatch of that shape would have satisfied the switch on paper and defeated it in substance. The three open items in this guard family are all classify-or-decide items whose deliverable IS a judgment, so the switch and the value scoring pointed the same way. The cost of a conductor who both does the work and verifies it is that there is no independent check -- which is exactly the cost that materialised on T-026, and exactly why the classification was also dispatched.

decisions.what: The acceptance clause that disqualifies "first match" and "last match" was settled by BUILDING both disqualified designs from the builder's own code and measuring them, rather than by reading the diff and agreeing it was neither.
decisions.why: This is the one clause a code review genuinely cannot settle. Any all-bindings implementation LOOKS non-positional -- it says filter(...).length === 0 -- and the question the acceptance actually asks is a behavioural one: does the verdict change when the two contradictory claims swap places? Deriving F_FIRST (bindings.slice(0,1)) and F_LAST (bindings.slice(-1)) from FIX holds the comparison machinery identical and varies ONLY position, so the difference in outcome is attributable to position and nothing else. The result is sharper than the acceptance anticipated: F_FIRST is silent on G1/G3/G6 and reproduces HEAD exactly, F_LAST is silent on G2, and each is blind precisely where the other sees. That is what upgrades the claim from "the fix catches the filed case" -- which F_LAST also does -- to "the fix catches the case AND its mirror", which no positional design can. decisions.what: The fix was authorised to land in the SHARED helper, closing the sibling C1 (`entries`) hole that T-029's acceptance never named -- and the authorisation was written into the SEALED pre-dispatch file, before the builder was told anything.

decisions.what: The builder's volunteered uncertainty about the clause-scoped digit window was MEASURED as a new gate cell (G12) rather than filed as a suspicion -- and it found a residual SILENT path, which was filed as T-031 at priority 3 while T-029 was still accepted.

decisions.what: The sealed prediction was NOT refuted, and the one place it was understated is recorded rather than smoothed over: it predicted the new false rejection would hit C2, and the measurement shows it hits C1 as well (2 failures, not 1).

decisions.what: T-031 is CLOSED as BOUNDARY and its defect is LEFT OPEN as KI-10, on a measurement the conductor made rather than on the builder's account of its own rejected work. The decision recorded here is deliberately TWO decisions: the item closes, and the defect stays open and visible. The real remedy is not a third narrowing but KI-9 option 2 -- give the counts real structure in the README so the guard stops reading English -- which is a README change, out of this run's builder file scope, and a human's call.

decisions.what: KI-8 is mitigated by COMMIT-REVEAL rather than by a hidden path: the sealed gate design was written, sha256-committed, and its plaintext DELETED from disk for the entire dispatch window, then rewritten and checked with `sha256sum -c` (OK) after the builder returned.

The obvious fix, hiding the file in /tmp (unreachable to subagents per KI-6), is NOT available: /tmp is denied to the conductor's Write tool. Commit-reveal is strictly stronger anyway. A file that does not exist during the dispatch window cannot be read by any means, and the pre-dispatch hash still binds the conductor against retro-fitting predictions to results. The cost is that a session death between seal and reveal loses the plaintext; the hash would then prove only that a seal existed. Accepted, and journaled.

decisions.what: The cycle-36 gate FAILED on its own check C9 at first run, and the failure was in the GATE, not the code. C9's exception set was amended from {H1} to {H1, H8} and the gate re-run to PASS.

The SEALED document predicted, in writing and before dispatch, "H8 ... GREEN@WORK"; its C9 line then said "except H1 (the one intended flip)". Had the seal predicted H8 RED@WORK and the run produced GREEN, the honest outcome would have been a FAILED gate and T-027 back to todo. decisions.what: T-033 ACCEPTED with three conductor discriminators recorded as FAILED, and the acceptance cell that passed is labelled WEAK EVIDENCE in the same breath.

The acceptance was in the dispatch prompt, so cell C1 passing cannot distinguish a general fix from one fitted to the clause -- this is hard rule 2's hazard (an agent that knows the check can code to the check) arriving through an ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE rather than through a verify command, a channel this run had not previously guarded. Discriminator D1, authored after the return and using phrasing named by neither the item nor the marker list, is the real measurement of the LOUD direction, and it FIRED -- so that direction is narrowed, not closed (T-034). The item still passes, and the reason is D4, a discriminator no clause asked for: move the acknowledgement verbatim to another section and the ack test fires on WORK while HEAD stays silent. The scoping half is therefore real, new, and wording-independent, which is where the durable value is; the widening half is a finite enumeration and was disclosed as such by the builder before any gate ran. Accepting on the half that generalises, while filing the half that does not, is the honest split.

decisions.what: Gate check D4 was found to be measuring nothing and was RE-ANCHORED mid-verification; its v1 result (FAIL) is discarded as a harness defect rather than reported as a finding about the item.
decisions.why: D4 claims to move the genuine acknowledgement OUT of the Tag vocabulary section, and v1 inserted it before the '\n## Exit codes' anchor -- which is the heading IMMEDIATELY AFTER Tag vocabulary, so the 'moved' sentence landed at the END of the very section it claimed to have left. The failure direction was the DANGEROUS one this time: v1 manufactured a FAIL that would have counted against the item, i.e. the mirror image of c19's manufactured KILLED. D1, D2 and D3 stayed FAILED as authored and were not touched.

decisions.what: Sealed prediction G4's HEAD arm was REFUTED by my own gate and is recorded as wrong.
decisions.why: The cycle-37 seal (.swarm/runs/cycle-037-precommit.md, sha256 committed before dispatch, plaintext withheld for the whole dispatch window, `sha256sum -c` OK on reveal) predicted the moved-acknowledgement cell would be RED on BOTH arms. It cuts the useful way too: the refutation is what turned D4 into the gate's strongest positive evidence, since a cell both arms fail proves nothing about the fix while one only WORK catches proves the scoping is new.

decisions.what: T-035 accepted as done with the silent hole still open in narrower form, on the pass rule written into the sealed gate BEFORE dispatch: close the residual, or document it at the assertion site with a measurement.

decisions.what: Allocator posture flipped trickle -> HALTED this cycle (runs/allocator.json: trickle cap of 4% spent, allow_overall_pct 0, allow_premium_pct 0). Conductor response: continue the run, dispatch ZERO agents while halted. Cycle 39 ran entirely conductor-inline at zero subagent burn.
decisions.why: The rule is genuinely silent here and the gap is filed as KI-13 rather than guessed around. bin/swarm-pacer.sh line 104 skips on posture=halted, but that skip sits in the AUTO-KICKOFF path -- it decides whether to start a NEW run, not whether an in-flight run's cycles proceed, and the pacer demonstrably spawned this cycle immediately after logging posture=halted. So halted does not formally stop this run. It does mean the swarm's weekly trickle allowance is fully spent, with weekly_used_pct 93 and opus 97 against a week that resets at 1786942799 -- AFTER stop_at 1786879464, so the window cannot recover before the run ends. Continuing to dispatch builders for the remaining ~9.8h would spend past a cap the operator set. Early WRAP_UP was considered and REJECTED as overreach: cycle.md's WRAP_UP triggers are the clock, all-targets-stalled, or a control stop, and none fired -- scaling the run down on a signal whose semantics are undefined is the user's call, not the conductor's. The middle path is the conservative one the silence permits: keep cycling, do conductor-only work (planning, backlog hygiene, docs, test triage -- all gear-1 sanctioned), spend no agent tokens.

decisions.what: Held at ZERO AGENTS for a second cycle even though the allocator posture flipped halted -> trickle and the pacer spawned the cycle on that basis. The permission to resume was measured to be an ARTIFACT of a SWARM tooling bug, and the run declined to spend on it.
decisions.why: bin/swarm-allocator.sh detects a week rollover with an exact integer comparison, `[ "$WRST" -ne "$S_WRST" ]`, against week_resets_at from the usage probe. That value is NOT stable to the integer second: the API returns seven_day.resets_at as a sub-second timestamp that straddles a whole-second boundary, and 25 samples over 125s this cycle returned BOTH 1786942799 and 1786942800 (runs/cycle-040-resets-jitter.json; four consecutive 5s samples caught the crossing live at 04:59:59.954603 -> 05:00:00.110580). At 02:16:47 the stored 1786942799 met a probed 1786942800, the rollover branch fired, and it wiped ALL attribution -- human_used_pct, swarm_used_pct, and critically trickle_used_pct 4 -> 0, the cap whose exhaustion had produced cycle 39's halted posture. The real week does not reset until 1786942800 = 2026-08-17T05:00Z, roughly 26.7h out and well AFTER stop_at 1786879464, so no week rolled over and the 4% trickle allowance is still genuinely spent. Taking the flip at face value would launder a bug into permission to burn. The independent numbers agree: weekly_used_pct 93 against week_elapsed_pct 84.09, opus_used_pct 97. The asymmetry decided it -- holding costs some foregone builder work on internal test guards no CLI user will ever see; resuming spends against a spent allowance on an account at 97% premium. Filed as KI-14; NOT fixed live (hard rule 5 fences bin/).

decisions.what: THE NON-DISCRIMINATION FINDING: the prose-anchor guard family's failure signature carries no information a maintainer can act on. A TRUE sentence and a FALSE sentence in the same wording frame produce byte-identical suite output -- same isolated counts, same full-suite counts, same failing test name.
decisions.why: Reached independently on two different guards, each with its own paired failable control. Band-count guard: B1 "Of 37 tags, 4 tags carry 5+ entries each:" (both figures true) and B2 (count 5, genuinely wrong) both give isolated pass=3 fail=1, full 79/1, same name. Attribution guards: A3 "Fewer than 9 are rated HIGH." (true, 8 < 9) and A5 "Fewer than 7 are rated HIGH." (false) are identical; A4 "Fewer than 51 entries are listed." (true, 50 < 51) and A6 (false) are identical. A3/A4 were authored specifically to remove the one soft spot in the first pass -- cell A1's truth rested on an unsettled fact about the triage doc, so the finding was re-derived on sentences true by arithmetic from figures the suite itself derives from source. THIS STRENGTHENS THE CYCLE-25 STANDING FINDING RATHER THAN RESTATING IT. Cycle 25 held that the failure direction was safe because these guards reject a correct README loudly rather than passing a wrong one silently. That is measured true and is now measured INCOMPLETE: loudness without discrimination is not a safe failure, because the maintainer who trips it cannot diagnose it as false, and their cheapest correct-looking action is deleting the guard -- which is precisely the cumulative risk cycle 25 named. The argument for T-024 no longer rests on aesthetics about prose anchors; it rests on a measured property of the failure signal.

decisions.what: T-026 closed as a documented BOUNDARY with its HOLE branch REFUTED by measurement; T-024b and T-032 deliberately left OPEN on the same evidence.
decisions.why: The three items are one family and it would have been cheap to close all three the way cycle 39 closed four. The distinction is what the measurement actually settles. T-026 asked a QUESTION WITH A MEASURABLE ANSWER -- is this a silent hole? -- and its acceptance made the HOLE branch conditional on the suite going GREEN. It does not go green (C1 78/2), and cell C2 shows a row deletion under that layout is still caught by T-019 exactly as in the C3 isolating control, so nothing is masked. T-024b and T-032 ask whether a STRUCTURAL derivation exists that keeps every kill; the measurement proves their false rejections are real and non-discriminating, but it does not establish that no structural reading exists, and their acceptances demand BOUNDARY be argued against a measurement rather than asserted. Extending the T-026 verdict to them would be exactly the move cycle 39 named and refused when it declined to extend the acknowledgement-guard verdict to extractions it had not measured.

decisions.what: Wave autotune NOT applied; k_current stays 5, wave_streak stays 0. Churn breaker: consecutive_no_value stays 0.
